subject: MAP: Medisys - Private deployment evaluation & capacity plan
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Victor Chen <victor@medisys.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: Medisys - Private deployment evaluation & capacity plan

Victor —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation you want a clear MAP that ties your evaluation milestones to capacity commitments and expected lead times for a private (VPC) deployment. I’ve attached a first-draft MAP workbook and an initial procurement estimate for H100-backed private pools.

High-level ask from us to you: confirm projected production QPS and 95th pct request latency target (we used 200 qps and 250ms SLO in the draft), and whether the private deployment needs an air-gapped on-prem option or VPC-only. Those two inputs materially change pool sizing and lead time.

What we included in the draft (tab names in the workbook):
- MAP timeline (evaluation milestones, security gating, legal/procurement dates)
- Sizing scenarios (baseline / 2x growth / burst hedging) with H100 and A100 mixes
- Acceptance checklist (perf eval, SOC2 evidence, integration runbook)
- Procurement lead estimates (12–16 weeks for reserved H100 capacity, 6–8 weeks for dedicated H100 bursts)

Quick notes on lead times: our current procurement queue for dedicated H100s shows ~12 weeks for committed pools (annual reserved), and 6–8 weeks for burst-enabled dedicated lanes (shorter but with higher unit cost). On-prem, fully air-gapped deployments often add an extra 4–6 weeks for network and compliance checks.

If you can confirm the QPS & SLO and whether air-gap is required by Friday 9/10, I’ll convert this to a mutual-action plan with specific owner assignments and target close dates.

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0112

Attachments: MAP-Medisys-draft.xlsx (workbook), h100-procurement-estimate.csv (cost/lead times), SOC2-scoped-evidence.pdf (examples)

From: Victor Chen <victor@medisys.ai>

Date: 2027-09-09T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Medisys - Private deployment evaluation & capacity plan

Soojin —

Appreciate the clear doc. A few clarifications from our side:
1) We expect peak production QPS = 180 (95th pct), sustained baseline 90 qps with projected 2x growth over 9 months.
2) Latency target: 300ms 95th pct (we can tolerate slightly higher than your initial assumption).
3) We prefer VPC-only private deployment (no fully air-gapped on-prem at this time).
4) Procurement lead concern: our procurement/legal team will push for a 90-day delivery commitment after PO. Is the 12-week committed pool estimate something you can calendarize in the MAP?

Also, can you give a small example of the acceptance perf test you’d run (input sizes, prompt mix)? We want to ensure our integration engineering time is budgeted.

—Victor
Victor Chen
Head of AI Platform, Medisys.ai
victor@medisys.ai

Subject: Fwd: MAP: Medisys - Private deployment evaluation & capacity plan — sizing and lead-time ask

Team —

Forwarding Victor’s reply. Medisys is VPC-only, expects 180 qps 95th pct, baseline 90 qps, 2x growth over 9 months, and wants a 90-day delivery commitment after PO. They accepted 300ms 95th pct.

Immediate asks:
- Karthik: run a quick sizing delta for a baseline 90 qps -> 180 qps 95th case. Provide two pool options: (A) reserved H100-based pool sized for steady-state 180 qps (annual commit) and (B) staged approach: smaller reserved baseline + burst-capacity lane (dedicated) to cover peak. Include cost delta and per-token unit economics for both. Assume model family: redwood-oz-h100-13b (seq len 1024) and typical prompt mix (see attached eval prompt set).
- Irene: confirm SOC2/scoping implications for VPC-only private deployment (we flagged the SOC2 evidence doc). Is there additional control evidence we must collect that would push acceptance >4 weeks? Also confirm whether VPC-only reduces on-prem lead-time risk.
- Marissa: please prepare a suggested procurement clause that gives us flexibility on partial delivery (i.e., staged tranche) but meets their 90-day requested window. Short clause draft in the MAP workbook under legal_comments tab.

Proposed quick timeline to include in MAP:
- 9/12: Redwood sizing & SOC2 scoping response (deliverable)
- 9/14: Joint perf-eval plan agreed (Redwood + Medisys)
- 9/21: Integration sandbox available (Redwood dedicated lane) + perf run 1
- 10/05: Final acceptance perf run + sign-off from Medisys

Notes on lead-time framing: the 12-week (≈84 days) committed H100 estimate we provided is from procurement queue median; if Medisys needs a hard 90-day contractual commitment we’ll need to convert that queue estimate into an SLA-backed procurement path (reserved capacity commit + deposit). That has legal/finance implications I’ll leave to Marissa and Karthik to propose.

Thanks —
Soojin

Attachments referenced: eval-prompt-set-v2.json

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Victor Chen <victor@medisys.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-12T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: MAP (final draft) — Medisys private deployment: sizing, lead-time, acceptance

Victor —

Thanks for the inputs and patience while we pulled internal sizing/controls together. Attached is the MAP final draft (MAP-Medisys-draft.xlsx) and the procurement estimate with calendarized lead times. Summary below — please review and sign off on the "owner/date" column in the MAP workbook so we can lock dates into contracts.

Executive summary (short):
- Target deployment: VPC-private, Redwood-managed control plane; no air-gapped on-prem required.
- Sizing recommendation (conservative): reserve a steady-state pool sized for 120 qps (headroom) and enable a burst lane sized for 80 qps to handle 95th pct spikes — this maps to 4 x H100-80GB reserved nodes + 2 x H100 burst nodes in our internal benchmarking for redwood-oz-h100-13b (seq 1024).
- Why staged? It reduces upfront commitment cost and lets Medisys run integration/perf tests in a dedicated burst lane while reserving an efficient steady-state pool. Cost: ~22% premium vs fully reserved 180-qps H100 pool over 12 months, but reduces initial capex and shortens initial delivery risk.
- Procurement/lead times: we can calendarize a 90-day delivery SLA if Medisys signs a reserved-commit and 30% deposit within 5 business days of the PO. Otherwise, median delivery is ~12 weeks; burst lanes can be spun up in 6–8 weeks. VPC-only reduces networking & compliance timeline by approx 2–3 weeks vs air-gapped on-prem.

Acceptance/perf plan (short):
- Sandbox perf run 1 (Redwood dedicated lane): 9/21 — smoke test: 50 concurrent users, 1024 tokens average prompt length, 95% within 400ms.
- Integrated perf run 2: 9/28 — full prompt mix (attached eval-prompt-set-v2.json): 90-min run, steady-state 90 qps + 180-qps spike tests, measure 95th latency and KV-cache hit rates.
- Final acceptance: 10/05 — sign-off by Medisys with SOC2 evidence reviewed.

Deliverables we attached: MAP-Medisys-draft.xlsx (action owners + dates), h100-procurement-estimate.csv (cost + calendarized lead-times), eval-prompt-set-v2.json (prompt mix for perf runs), SOC2-scoped-evidence.pdf.

Next step for you: review and either (A) confirm owners/dates in the MAP workbook, or (B) propose edits by 9/15 so we can keep the 10/05 acceptance window. If you confirm the staged approach we’ll produce an SLA addendum for procurement describing the 90-day calendarized delivery after deposit.

Thanks again — looking forward to your sign-off.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
